q: Which James Bond film popularised the phrase 'shaken, not stirred'?
o: It runs through the series, first spoken on screen in Goldfinger
r: Bond orders it in the novels, and the exact screen phrasing lands in Goldfinger. Purists note shaking a Martini is technically wrong.

q: In Mad Men, which drink is Don Draper most associated with?
r: The Old Fashioned, which the show helped revive for a new generation.

q: The Cosmopolitan's 1990s boom is widely credited to which TV show?
r: Sex and the City made it the decade's defining cocktail.

q: 'The Dude' in The Big Lebowski drinks which cocktail?
r: The White Russian, which he calls a Caucasian.

q: Which cocktail features in the title of a famous Jimmy Buffett song?
r: Margaritaville. Rupert Holmes handled the Piña Colada.

q: 'Escape (The Piña Colada Song)' was recorded by whom?
r: Rupert Holmes, 1979. The song is actually about a couple answering each other's personal ads.

q: Which Bollywood song title references a drink measure?
o: Songs referencing 'peg' are common in Punjabi pop
r: Punjabi and Bollywood pop reference 'peg' frequently, reflecting how deeply the word sits in Indian drinking slang.

q: Which drink is associated with New Orleans' Mardi Gras and its Hurricane glass?
r: The Hurricane, though the Sazerac, Ramos Gin Fizz and Vieux Carré are all New Orleans classics too.

q: The Vieux Carré cocktail is named after what?
o: The French Quarter of New Orleans
r: Vieux Carré is the French Quarter, where it was created at the Hotel Monteleone.

q: Which cocktail is traditionally served at the Kentucky Derby?
r: The Mint Julep, by the tens of thousands.

q: Which drink is the traditional choice at Wimbledon alongside strawberries?
r: Pimm's No. 1 with lemonade, fruit and mint.

q: Which cocktail shares its name with a Manhattan borough?
r: All three are real cocktails: the Bronx, the Brooklyn and the Queens Park Swizzle. A question where the options aren't mutually exclusive.

q: The Bee's Knees cocktail dates from which era, and why the name?
o: Prohibition, when honey masked rough bathtub gin
Victorian London, named for a beekeeper
r: Gin, honey and lemon. The honey helped hide the taste of poor-quality Prohibition gin.

q: Which spirit does a Sidecar use?
r: Cognac with Cointreau and lemon.

q: What is the 'Death in the Afternoon' cocktail, and who created it?
o: Absinthe and champagne, attributed to Hemingway
Rum and absinthe, by Trader Vic
Gin and champagne, by Harry Craddock
Whiskey and absinthe, by Jerry Thomas
r: Absinthe topped with champagne, attributed to Hemingway and named after his bullfighting book.

q: Jerry Thomas is significant to cocktail history because he did what?
o: Published the first bartender's guide in 1862
r: 'How to Mix Drinks; or, The Bon Vivant's Companion' (1862) is the first known cocktail book.

q: The Savoy Cocktail Book was written by whom?
r: Harry Craddock of the American Bar at the Savoy, 1930. Ada Coleman preceded him there and created the Hanky Panky.

q: Ada Coleman, one of history's most famous bartenders, created which drink?
r: The Hanky Panky, at the Savoy's American Bar. Dick Bradsell created the Bramble decades later.

q: The Bramble was created in 1980s London by which bartender?
r: Dick Bradsell, who also gave us the Espresso Martini.

q: Which is true of the Ramos Gin Fizz?
o: It is shaken for a famously long time to build its foam
r: Gin, cream, egg white, citrus and orange flower water, shaken at length for that cloud-like head.

q: Which trend defined cocktail bars in the 2010s?
o: The craft cocktail revival with house syrups, clarification and low-waste bars
r: House-made everything, historical revivals, and later a sustainability push against waste.

q: What is the 'low- and no-alcohol' trend driven by?
o: Health-conscious drinkers wanting the ritual without the alcohol
Higher taxes on strong spirits only
r: Sober-curious drinking pushed distilled non-alcoholic spirits and serious zero-alcohol menus into the mainstream.

q: What does 'sober curious' mean?
o: Choosing to drink less or not at all without identifying as fully sober
Abstaining one month a year only
r: A cultural shift toward moderation, which reshaped bar menus worldwide.

q: What is a 'low-waste' or 'closed-loop' bar?
o: A bar that uses citrus husks, peels and offcuts instead of binning them
A bar that serves only local spirits
A bar with no single-use glassware
A bar that never batches drinks
r: Husk cordials, oleo-saccharum from peels, and reusing every part of an ingredient.

q: What is oleo-saccharum?
o: Sugar-extracted citrus peel oil, used in punches
r: Sugar draws the oil out of citrus peels, creating an intensely aromatic syrup used in classic punches.

q: Which is true of the modern 'highball renaissance', especially in Japan?
o: Whisky highballs are treated with precision on ice, dilution and carbonation
It refers to taller glassware only
It means highballs made with sparkling wine
It is a return to pre-mixed cans only
r: Japanese bars turned the highball into a discipline: hard ice, cold soda, exact ratios, minimal stirring.

q: What is 'clarified milk punch' prized for?
o: A silky texture and long shelf life with a clear appearance
r: The milk curdles, is strained out, and leaves a clear, velvety drink that keeps for months.

q: Which is a genuine trend in Indian bars in recent years?
o: Regional Indian ingredients in classic templates
A ban on all imported spirits
A shift away from whisky entirely
r: Kokum, gondhoraj, jamun, curry leaf and toddy appearing in sours, spritzes and highballs.

q: What does 'terroir' mean when applied to spirits?
o: The influence of place, climate and raw material on flavour
r: Borrowed from wine: place shapes flavour, whether in agave, cane or grain.

q: Which is a rising category globally, especially among younger drinkers?
r: RTDs have grown fast for convenience and consistent quality.

q: What is 'agave spirit' terminology likely to include beyond tequila and mezcal?
r: Raicilla and bacanora are agave spirits with their own regions; sotol comes from a related plant.

q: What is the significance of the 'Death & Co' and 'PDT' bars?
o: They shaped the modern New York craft cocktail movement
They created the first RTD cocktails
r: Both are landmarks of the 2000s New York cocktail renaissance, and their books shaped bars worldwide.

q: Which best describes the 'World's 50 Best Bars' list?
o: An annual global ranking that has included Indian bars in recent years
A list of the oldest bars in the world
A ranking of bar sales volume
r: Indian bars have begun appearing on it, a marker of how fast the scene has matured.

q: What does 'batching for service' solve in a busy bar?
o: Speed and consistency across many drinks
r: Pre-measured mixes mean every drink tastes the same and lands fast.

q: Which is true of barrel-aged cocktails?
o: The whole cocktail rests in wood, softening and integrating it
Only the base spirit is aged
They must be aged for a year minimum
r: Ageing a Negroni or Manhattan in wood rounds it out; vermouth-containing drinks are common candidates.

q: What is the purpose of a 'garnish' in serious bartending?
r: A mint sprig or citrus twist sits at the nose and changes every sip. If it does neither, leave it off.

q: Which claim about the Manhattan is correct?
o: Rye or bourbon, sweet vermouth and bitters, stirred
Rye, dry vermouth and bitters, shaken
Whiskey, sweet vermouth and citrus, shaken
r: 2:1 whiskey to sweet vermouth with bitters, stirred and served up or on a cube.

q: The Boulevardier differs from a Negroni how?
r: Bourbon or rye in place of gin, often with a slightly higher whiskey proportion.

q: Which is true of the Americano cocktail?
r: The Negroni's ancestor: Campari, sweet vermouth and soda water.

q: What is 'Suze'?
r: A bitter French gentian-root aperitif, distinctively earthy.

q: Fernet-Branca is best described as what?
o: An intensely bitter Italian amaro, popular as a bartender's shot
r: Fiercely bitter and menthol-driven, famously the 'bartender's handshake'.

q: Which is true of the Paloma?
o: Tequila with grapefruit soda and lime
r: Mexico's everyday tequila drink, far more common there than the Margarita.

q: What is 'chilli-salt rim' or Tajín used for?
o: A savoury-spicy rim on Mexican-style drinks
A garnish for tiki drinks only
r: Chilli, lime and salt seasoning, used on Micheladas, Palomas and fruit.

q: A Michelada is built on what?
o: Beer with lime, salt and savoury seasonings
r: Mexican beer cocktail: lime, salt, hot sauce and sometimes clamato.

q: What distinguishes a Caipirinha from a Daiquiri?
o: Cachaça and muddled lime wheels rather than rum and lime juice
r: Cachaça, muddled lime and sugar, built in the glass over crushed ice.

q: Singani, a lesser-known grape spirit, comes from which country?
r: Bolivia, distilled from high-altitude Muscat grapes.

q: Which is true of aquavit?
o: A Scandinavian spirit flavoured with caraway or dill
r: Caraway or dill-forward, traditionally drunk with food in Scandinavia.

q: What is 'raki' and where is it from?
r: Turkey's anise spirit, which turns cloudy with water, like ouzo and pastis.

q: Why do anise spirits like raki, ouzo and pastis turn cloudy with water?
o: The louche effect: anise oils are insoluble in water and form an emulsion
r: Called the louche. Essential oils drop out of solution, clouding the glass.

q: Which best describes 'navy strength' spirits?
o: Bottled at 57% ABV or above, historically so spilled spirit wouldn't ruin gunpowder
r: 57% was the 'proof' point at which gunpowder soaked in spirit would still ignite.

q: Which is true of sherry styles?
o: Fino is dry and pale; Pedro Ximénez is intensely sweet
r: Fino and manzanilla are dry and delicate; oloroso is richer; PX is dessert-sweet.

q: Which is true of the Tommy's Margarita?
o: It replaces triple sec with agave syrup
r: Created at Tommy's in San Francisco: tequila, lime and agave nectar, no orange liqueur.

q: What is the difference between crème de cacao and chocolate liqueur in practice?
o: Crème de cacao is typically drier and used in classics like the Alexander
r: Crème de cacao (white or dark) is the classic cocktail ingredient; modern chocolate liqueurs are often sweeter and richer.

q: Which is true of Irish cream liqueurs in cocktails?
o: Acid can curdle them, which is why layered shots are drunk quickly
r: That's exactly why an Irish Slammer is drunk straight down before it curdles in the stout.
